logline: On Christmas Eve, miserly Ebenezer Scrooge is warned by his dead partner’s ghost and visited by three spirits who force him to confront his past, present, and possible future—so he may yet keep Christmas in his heart.

source_grounded_timeline.event: Scrooge works in cold fog; refuses nephew’s dinner; rebuffs charity gentlemen; grudgingly gives Cratchit Christmas Day off.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: Once upon a time—of all the good days in the year, on Christmas Eve—old Scrooge sat busy in his counting-house.

source_grounded_timeline.event: Marley’s face appears in the knocker; Marley’s Ghost enters in chains and warns of three Spirits.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: Scrooge, having his key in the lock of the door, saw in the knocker, without its undergoing any intermediate process of change—not a knocker, but Marley's face.

source_grounded_timeline.event: Ghost of Christmas Past shows lonely boy Scrooge, sister Fan, Fezziwig’s ball, and the lost fiancée’s release.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: Expect the first to-morrow, when the bell tolls One.

source_grounded_timeline.event: Ghost of Christmas Present shows London cheer, the Cratchit dinner, Tiny Tim’s frailty, and Ignorance and Want.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: I am the Ghost of Christmas Present,

source_grounded_timeline.when: When the last stroke of Twelve has ceased
source_grounded_timeline.event: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows indifference to a dead man, plunder of his goods, Cratchit grief, and a neglected grave.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: The third upon the next night when the last stroke of Twelve has ceased to vibrate.

source_grounded_timeline.event: Scrooge awakes reformed; sends prize turkey to Cratchits; pledges to charity; dines with nephew; raises Bob’s salary.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.

withheld_name_rules.description: Do not identify the unmourned dead man as Scrooge until the grave inscription is revealed.
withheld_name_rules.source_evidence: read upon the stone of the neglected grave his own name, EBENEZER SCROOGE.

withheld_name_rules.description: Marley’s death is established at the open; his return as Ghost is the first wonder and must not be spoiled by early spectral staging outside the knocker beat.
withheld_name_rules.source_evidence: Marley was dead: to begin with. There is no doubt whatever about that.

essential_beats.name: Marley dead; Scrooge alone and cold
essential_beats.why_essential: Establishes the premise that nothing wonderful follows unless Marley’s death is believed.
essential_beats.source_evidence: This must be distinctly understood, or nothing wonderful can come of the story I am going to relate.

essential_beats.name: Nephew’s Merry Christmas refused
essential_beats.why_essential: States Scrooge’s war on Christmas and family.

essential_beats.name: Charity refused; surplus population
essential_beats.why_essential: Gives the moral crime later thrown back at him.
essential_beats.source_evidence: If they would rather die," said Scrooge, "they had better do it, and decrease the surplus population.

essential_beats.name: Marley’s chain and warning
essential_beats.why_essential: Inciting supernatural contract: three Spirits or Marley’s fate.
essential_beats.source_evidence: You will be haunted," resumed the Ghost, "by Three Spirits."

essential_beats.name: Past: neglected child and lost love
essential_beats.why_essential: Shows origin of hardness and the cost of Gain.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Another idol has displaced me; and if it can cheer and comfort you in time to come, as I would have tried to do, I have no just cause to grieve.

essential_beats.name: Present: Cratchit feast and Tiny Tim
essential_beats.why_essential: Human stakes; Scrooge hears his own cruel words quoted.
essential_beats.source_evidence: God bless us every one!" said Tiny Tim, the last of all.

essential_beats.name: Future: lonely death and the grave
essential_beats.why_essential: Climax of fear and choice; name withheld until stone.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Am I that man who lay upon the bed?" he cried, upon his knees.

essential_beats.name: End of it: amendment
essential_beats.source_evidence: and to Tiny Tim, who did NOT die, he was a second father.

scene_outline.heading: INT. SCROOGE AND MARLEY COUNTING-HOUSE – CHRISTMAS EVE
scene_outline.purpose: Establish Scrooge’s coldness; nephew, charity, clerk.
scene_outline.source_evidence: The door of Scrooge's counting-house was open that he might keep his eye upon his clerk, who in a dismal little cell beyond, a sort of tank, was copying letters.

scene_outline.heading: EXT./INT. SCROOGE’S YARD AND CHAMBERS – NIGHT
scene_outline.source_evidence: I wear the chain I forged in life," replied the Ghost.

scene_outline.heading: INT. BEDROOM / PAST VISIONS – SPIRIT TIME
scene_outline.purpose: Past Spirit; boyhood loneliness; Belle’s release.
scene_outline.source_evidence: I am the Ghost of Christmas Past.

scene_outline.heading: INT. TRANSFORMED CHAMBERS / CRATCHIT HOME / STREETS – SPIRIT TIME
scene_outline.purpose: Present Spirit; Cratchit Christmas; Tim’s fate conditional.
scene_outline.source_evidence: If these shadows remain unaltered by the Future, the child will die.

scene_outline.heading: EXT./INT. CITY, EXCHANGE, RAG-AND-BOTTLE SHOP, BED, CHURCHYARD – SPIRIT TIME
scene_outline.purpose: Silent Future; death without mourning; grave reveal.
scene_outline.source_evidence: Before I draw nearer to that stone to which you point," said Scrooge, "answer me one question.

scene_outline.heading: INT./EXT. CHAMBERS, STREETS, NEPHEW’S, COUNTING-HOUSE – CHRISTMAS DAY
scene_outline.purpose: Joyful reform; turkey; charity; Fred; raise for Bob.
scene_outline.source_evidence: Best and happiest of all, the Time before him was his own, to make amends in!
